newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Orion says earnings may level off. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Finnish Orion says earnings may level off. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]

text.p: (Company corrects headline and wording of earlier statement).
Finnish pharmaceuticals group Orion-Yhtyma Oy said on Tuesday its net sales and operating profit may level off.
"It is ... anticipated that the Orion group net sales and operating profit may level off," Orion said in a corrected statement.
In 1996, net sales grew 5.5 percent to 4.28 billion markka from 4.06 billion in 1995, and profit before extraordinary items and tax rose 10.3 percent to 738 million markka, Orion said.
Growth of the Finnish pharmaceuticals market was expected to slow down, and the outlook for overseas sales was uncertain, it said.

The timetables for registration and launching of the group's patented drugs in the U.S. and Europe were difficult to predict, Orion said, adding that payments based on its marketing agreements were linked to these timetables.
Although sales growth picked up towards the end of 1996, the full-year growth was not entirely up to expectations, Orion said.
